newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Northland receives offer for operations.
newsitem.headline: Northland receives offer for operations.

text.p: Northland Port Corp (NZ) Ltd said on Friday it had received an unsolicited offer to buy all its engineering operations in Auckland and Whangarei as going concerns.
Chairman Jim Hardie said the offer covered 100 percent of Marine Steel Ltd, which operates engineering workshops, a ship repair yard and slipway in Auckland.
It also covers 100 percent of Northport Engineering ltd, which also has major engineering workshops, ship repair facilities slipways at Port Whangarei.
Hardie said NPC had been investigating possible options for reorganising Marine Steel's Auckland operations.

"During this process we have received an unsolicited offer to buy all of our engineering operations as going concerns, and we have agreed to allow that prospective purchaser to undertake due diligence studies."
Due diligence will proceed during June and a decision is likely by the end of July, Hardie said.
"I must stress that no decision has yet been made on this matter, whether we will accept any purchase offer or proceed with some reorganisation ourselves," he said.
Hardie declined to discuss likely prices or to put a valuation on the businesses involved.
